N1 deviates from the validator’s wording. Its example rule (judge a line by the next line «that fits the lines before it») fails the validator’s own test «a back-dated line after real lines marks only itself» when real events are sparse. I simulated it (scratchpad/readrule-sim.mjs):
- real 10:00, 10:05, 10:10, then a back-dated 10:00: the two real lines were marked, the forged one was not;
- the same happens when the journal starts with a single real line.
So AC4 now uses a symmetric, content-only rule. A conflict is a pair where the later line in the file is more than 120 s earlier. While conflicts remain, mark the line in the most conflicts; on a tie, mark the later line in the file. Only the last line uses the clock. The ORCH ruling holds: marks depend only on content except for the last line; a forward-dated line is judged by the lines after it; the server appends in acceptance order; the same journal read at T and T+2 h gives the same marks.
Simulated (scratchpad/readrule-sim2.mjs):
- honest journals of 400 lines with ±59 s and gaps of 1, 20 and 600 s: 0 marks;
- the validator’s example (real 10:00, forged 11:00, then 10:01, 10:30, 10:59): only the forged line, at 10:59:30 and at 13:00;
- a back-dated line, dense and sparse: only itself;
- two forged future lines followed by three real lines: only the forged ones;
- a mixed journal: the same marks at T and T+2 h;
- a +1 h last line: marked by the clock rule (в).
One tie is documented in the description: two forged future lines followed by exactly two real lines marks the real ones until one more real line arrives. The rule is detection; the guard is the mandate (R2).

changes.change:
AC4’s read rule is rewritten:
- (а) source not REAL;
- (б) among REAL lines, a conflict is a pair where the later line in the file is more than 120 s earlier. While conflicts remain, mark the line in the most conflicts; on a tie, mark the later line in the file;
- (в) only the last line uses the clock (more than 60 s in the future).
Except for (в), marks depend only on content, and a journal of accepted lines has no conflicts. The criterion states that the server appends in acceptance order and that the 120 s threshold is twice the write tolerance.
Tests: accepted lines only, no marks; SIMULATION; a back-dated line (also after only two real lines 10 minutes apart); a +1 h line followed by an hour of real lines; the same journal read at T and T+2 h gives the same marks; the last line +1 h.
AC2 now says lines follow acceptance order, and 20 concurrent writes at −59..+59 s must stay unmarked (the test calls the same rule function as the page).
The description («Где что лежит») says the rule is detection, not protection, documents the tie case, and states the assumption that the clock is not set back. «Числа»: 120 s is the conflict threshold.
This deviates from the validator’s example rule, which the simulation showed marks real lines in the sparse case; details are in the summary.

AC6(в): a task without an end is «окончание не записано» if a server start or its session’s end came after the task began. A session end affects only tasks started before it, so after a resume with the same session_id, new tasks are «в работе». The test is: session end, SessionStart (resume) with the same session_id, subagent start; the task must be «в работе». AC6(г) now reads «при событии окончания сессии после её начала».
«Сбои» is reworded the same way.
New fact (12): resuming (--resume, --continue, /resume) keeps the session_id; only --fork-session gives a new one (cli-reference); SessionStart then carries source «resume», and SessionEnd can carry reason «resume» or «clear». The sources list now names --fork-session.
REQ-007: a running session is one with an event after the last server start whose last event is not a session end; a resumed session runs again. REQ-007 AC1’s test adds the same end, resume, start sequence.
